questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English speaking and nice weather

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Loved it!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: My UCPH coordinator did not provide much information, and nothing was available specifically to Sydney online

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We were showed around by a local USYD coordinator at the hospital which was nice

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: My supervising doctor was not used to having exchange students, so I didn't receive any information prior to leaving Denmark, which was unfortunate.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There is student accommodation available through the hospital, but this was not advertised through UCPH, USYD or the hospital. I only heard from previous UCPH students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Please consider this student dorm - it is only around 3000 a month (way cheaper than city centre), and it is very nice to live at the hospital where you will be attending.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A bit old, but good price.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We were referred by our local UCPH coordinator to USYD, and were then contacted several months later by a USYD coordinator to apply for our desired departments. She was, however, new to the international student placements, and placed us in one department for 12 weeks, although the usual agreement is 4 weeks in 3 departments.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We had a contact coordinator at USYD, but as I mentioned she was unfamiliar with the usual process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: We ended up having to negotiate our way to have a placement of six weeks in two departments, which was okay, but three departments would have been ideal.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Advocate for having three departments placements - this is what the local med students get as well, and what the departments are geared towards.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We were in a clinical placement, so not much academic teaching, apart from the doctor's training.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Clinical placement in the hospital.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Similar with clinical placement combined with theoretical seminars and workshops, but we were not really encouraged to participate in the local med student classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Six weeks in emergency medicine and six weeks in neurology.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Both departments were good! Emergency is very hands-on and you can get to see patients yourself (which is quite unusual for Australia, where even junior doctors spend their first few years just taking notes). Neurology at Concord is a very advanced department, and you can learn a lot from the very interesting specialists.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You can be randomly selected to get a health examination with a chest X Ray as part of the visa application. This is mandatory and costs 2000 DKK.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Rent is super expensive, so apply for the hospital student dorm! Groceries are more expensive but eating out is cheaper than in Denmark, especially cafés and coffee. You will want to spend money on trips and tours while you are there, so set aside money for traveling.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot was available, but we arrived 1 month into the semester, which was too late to join.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports, choir, theatre, fan clubs etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I heard all of it is fun if you arrive early enough for orientation week!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: So much to do in Sydney - beaches, coastal walks, sightseeing, national parks, many cute cafés and shopping. We also did weekend trips to Melbourne, Noosa and Cairns, all within a 3 hour flight, which is not too expensive.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, Australian culture is very laid back and Western.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Arrive early enough for orientation week in February.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Probably the hierarchy between doctors - the junior doctors in internal medicine departments only take notes and never get to examine patients, which means that medical students only get to observe. 
Also Sydney is an extremely multicultural city, so the language barrier between patients was quite unexpected.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their openness, love of nature and the socializing both before and after work.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Apply for the student housing and save so much money. It is only a 25 minute train ride outside of the city centre, and you will appreciate having that money for traveling.
2. Arrive early or leave after your placement - Australia is a once in a lifetime destination, and you will want to explore more than just Sydney while you are there.
3. Soak up the learning opportunities at Concord! You can volunteer for teaching seminars and be trained in ultrasound, emergency simulations etc.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Set aside enough time for the application documents, and get started on your health examinations well in advance.
Apply for scholarships.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to take a full consultation with a patient in English, write up a note, order the relevant workup in the local system and consult with the attending doctor.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to write my Master's thesis at night while being in the hospital full-time, and having my exam with a 10 hour time difference. Would not recommend!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
